::: {.why}
The optimization is trivial and the estimation is not, so the fastest way to see the real problem is to solve it correctly first and watch what it does.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Write mean-variance optimization as a convex program and solve it with CVXPY for a given risk aversion.
- Say which of the two inputs the solution is more sensitive to, and give the reason in terms of how each is estimated.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Read the CVXPY introduction and the portfolio optimization example, then write the problem yourself for the 25 Fama-French portfolios: maximise expected return minus risk aversion times variance, subject to weights summing to one. Trace the frontier by sweeping risk aversion.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Perturb the inputs: add 10 percent noise to the estimated mean vector and re-solve, then do the same for the covariance matrix. Report the average absolute weight change under each perturbation. The asymmetry between the two numbers is the whole of week 15.
:::
:::
